title: Which steps run once, each or all?
scenario: A studio will make 50 versions of one approved tea ad: 10 markets, 5 sizes each. You review the draft pipeline. The draft and the request list are our own examples, made up for this case. Use the exhibit.
exhibit:
MASTER (made up for this case):
  One approved ad and a brand rules page. A person approved both on Monday.

DRAFT PIPELINE (made up for this case):
  1 Localise the tagline for each of the 50 versions
  2 Render the image for each of the 50 versions
  3 Check each tagline
  4 Check each image
  5 Pack all files and send them to the client

REQUESTS ON THE BOARD (made up for this case):
  R1 New market: Poland, all 5 sizes
  R2 Resize: the approved German ad, new size 4:5

questions.prompt: Step 1 localises the tagline once for each of the 50 versions. What is the better scope?

options.text: Each version: fifty runs, because every image needs its own fresh translation of the tagline
options.explanation: The five sizes of one market share the same words. So 40 of the 50 runs would repeat work.

options.text: Each market: ten runs, because the words depend on the market and not on the picture size
options.explanation: Right. The words change with the market only. Ten runs are enough, and the five sizes of a market reuse the result.

options.text: Once: a single run for the whole job, because one translation can serve every market
options.explanation: Each market needs its own language. One run cannot make ten different taglines.

options.text: All: after the images exist, so the tagline can be fitted to each finished picture
options.explanation: The words come before the image. "All" is for steps that wait until every item has finished.

questions.prompt: Which pair of steps can run at the same time without waiting for each other?

options.text: Making an image and checking that same image, since a check never changes the picture
options.explanation: A check needs the image to exist first. It cannot run at the same time as the step that makes it.

options.text: Checking a tagline and rendering its image, since the check only reads a short line of text
options.explanation: The render uses the tagline. Run together, a wrong tagline would be drawn before the check can stop it.

options.text: Rendering the files and packing them, since packing only moves files from one folder
options.explanation: Packing needs every file to be finished. It is an "all" step and must wait.

options.text: Localising the tagline for Germany and for France, since neither one needs the other one
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says parallel runs help when tasks do not depend on each other. The ten markets are independent.

questions.prompt: The draft renders images (step 2) before it checks taglines (step 3). What is the problem?

options.text: A wrong tagline is already inside a finished image, so check the words before the render
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic describes checks, called gates, on intermediate steps. A cheap check on text should come before the costly render.

options.text: Nothing is wrong, since the image check at step 4 would find any wrong tagline anyway
options.explanation: It may find it, but only after the render was paid for. A cheap check before the render saves that money.

options.text: The tagline check is too slow and should go, because the image check already covers the words
options.explanation: The tagline check is quick and cheap. Without it you lose the gate and pay for renders that fail.

options.text: Every image should be rendered twice, so that a person can choose the better tagline later
options.explanation: Rendering twice doubles the cost and does not fix a wrong tagline. The check is the fix.

questions.prompt: Which Anthropic workflow fits sorting requests R1 and R2 onto different paths?

options.text: Voting: it runs the same request several times so that the outputs can be compared
options.explanation: Anthropic describes voting as running the same task several times. It does not sort requests.

options.text: Sectioning: it splits one task into independent parts that all run in parallel
options.explanation: Sectioning splits one task into parts. R1 and R2 are two different requests, not parts of one.

options.text: Routing: it classifies each input and sends it down a specialised path of its own
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says routing "classifies an input and directs it to a specialized followup task". R1 needs localising. R2 goes straight to the image step.

options.text: Prompt chaining: it sends every request through the same steps, one step after the other
options.explanation: A chain has fixed steps for every input. R2 should skip localising, so it needs a different path.
